test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-3) Official Paper (Held On: 14 June 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Decreasing returns to scale occurs when_______

options.text: an increase in all inputs (labour/capital) leads to a more than proportional increase in output
an increase in all inputs (labour/capital) leads to a less than proportional increase in output
a decrease in all inputs (labour/capital) leads to a more than proportional increase in output
a decrease in all inputs (labour/capital) leads to a less than proportional increase in output

solution:
The correct answer is __**an increase in all inputs (labour/capital) leads to a less than proportional increase in output.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **A decreasing return to scale occurs** **when the proportion of output is less than the desired increased input during the production process.**
 
• For example,
 
 
• **if the input is increased by 3 times, but the output is reduced 2 times,** the firm or economy has experienced decreasing returns to scale.
 
 
 
• Decreasing returns to scale occur if the **production process becomes less efficient as production is expanded.**
 
• As in case, a firm becomes too large to be managed effectively as a single unit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Returns to scale**

 
 
• Returns to scale are** the variation or change in productivity that is the outcome of a proportionate increase of all the input.**
 
• **​An increasing return to scale** occurs **when the output increases by a larger proportion than the increase in inputs** during the production process.
 
• For example,** if the input is increased by 3 times, but output increases by 3.75 times, then the firm or economy has experienced an increasing return to scale.**
